US-119-HR10890.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to establish the motor fuel deduction.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10890.aiSummary: The bill would create a new income tax deduction for individuals for personal motor fuel costs. It would cover gas, diesel, and the cost to recharge an electric vehicle for personal use, and it would also be available to people who do not itemize deductions. The changes would apply to amounts paid or incurred after December 31, 2026.

US-119-HR10791.title: Italian Heroes and Heritage Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10791.description: To prohibit Federal funds from being provided to any State or local government that celebrates Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10791.aiSummary: The bill would bar federal money from going to any state or local government that celebrates Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day. This would apply starting one year after October 12, 2026, and on each later Columbus Day. It also says Congress thinks October 12 should keep being observed nationwide as Columbus Day.

US-119-HR10670.title: China FIREWALL Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10670.description: To prohibit Chinese AI models from being used on government-issued devices or software systems, to prohibit the procurement of any such models, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10670.aiSummary: The bill would bar Chinese AI models from being used on federal government devices and software systems, and it would also stop executive agencies from buying those models or software that uses them. It would require federal standards and guidelines for removing covered apps from government technology within 60 days after enactment. The bill includes exceptions for law enforcement, national security, and security researchers, and it allows case-by-case waivers for national security reasons.

US-119-HR9340.title: Ratepayer Protection Act
US-119-HR9340.summary:
Ratepayer Protection Act

The bill requires state utility regulators and nonregulated utilities to consider implementing a standard to hold certain large-load customers responsible for the costs associated with any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade of electric service necessary to serve such customers. A large-load customer means a non-residential electric consumer that enters, or requests to enter, an agreement concerning the sale of electric energy primarily to operate information technology infrastructure and related systems pertaining to data storage and computational applications and services (e.g., data centers) that have a peak electric demand of 100 megawatts or more at a single site or campus.

Specifically, the bill requires states to consider implementing a federal standard for large-load customers. The standard must require rates charged by electric utilities for providing electric service to a large-load customer to be designed to recover from the large-load customer the full, incremental cost of any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade necessary to serve such customer. This rate must include the costs that would be incurred if the large-load customer terminates an agreement with the electric utility pertaining to the sale of electric energy or otherwise ceases the purchase of energy from the electric utility.

Under the standard, an electric utility must require the large-load customer to provide to the utility financial assurances or contributions to cover the cost of any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade that is necessary to serve the load of a large-load customer before the utility makes any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade.
US-119-HR9340.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Reported to House, 2026-09-10)

US-119-HR10593.title: Permanently Authorizing PILT Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10593.description: To amend section 6906 of title 31, United States Code, to permanently authorize the Payment in Lieu of Taxes program.
US-119-HR10593.aiSummary: The bill would permanently authorize the Payment in Lieu of Taxes program, which sends federal payments to help local governments that have land the government owns. It would change the law so the program can operate each fiscal year instead of only through fiscal year 2019.

US-119-HR10571.title: Surge to Save Newborns Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10571.description: To amend the Public Health Service Act with respect to State support for newborn screening, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10571.aiSummary: The bill would create a federal grant program to help states put newborn screening in place for conditions on the federal recommended screening list. State health leaders or state agencies could apply for the grants. It would set aside $35 million each year from 2027 through 2031 for these grants and require yearly reports to Congress on progress and results.

US-119-HR4093.title: Apples to Apples Comparison Act of 2025
US-119-HR4093.summary:
Apples to Apples Comparison Act of 2025

This bill requires additional reporting and disclosures regarding Medicare enrollment and expenditures.

Specifically, the bill requires the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to annually report on and publish information on its website regarding expenditures for Medicare hospital services and medical services, the Medicare prescription drug benefit, and Medicare Advantage (MA), including for those who are enrolled in one program but not others or have supplemental insurance. This information must be broken down by county and metropolitan statistical area for each month over the prior 10-year period and for each month over the next 5-year period.

In addition, the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission must annually analyze and report on expenditures for Medicare beneficiaries who have an MA plan compared to those who do not have an MA plan. The Boards of Trustees for Medicare must annually report on expenditures for (1) Medicare beneficiaries who have either hospital services or medical services but not both, and (2) Medicare beneficiaries who have both hospital and medical services but do not have an MA plan.
US-119-HR4093.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-06-24)

US-119-HR4093.aiSummary: The bill would require more public reports about Medicare enrollment and spending. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services would have to post yearly data on hospital care, doctor care, prescription drugs, and Medicare Advantage, broken down by county and metro area and by month. Medicare advisers and the Medicare trustees would also have to give yearly reports comparing costs for people with and without Medicare Advantage and for people with different parts of Medicare coverage.

US-119-HR10395.title: Critical Materials Future Act of 2025

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10395.description: To establish a pilot program to support domestic critical material processing, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10395.aiSummary: The bill would set up a pilot program at the Energy Department to support at least 3 domestic projects that refine, process, or recycle critical materials. It would use financial tools like price support to help these projects and to study how they affect supply chains and markets. The Energy Secretary would also have to issue rules, pick projects, and send annual reports to Congress.

US-119-HR10131.title: National Archives Protection Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10131.description: To amend title 44, United States Code, to prohibit the closure of Federal records centers, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10131.aiSummary: The bill would stop the Archivist from closing certain federal records centers and archive facilities that were already open before the law takes effect. It would also bar unreasonable limits on public access to those places. In some cases, it would forbid rebuilding or changing a facility if that would move records for more than 180 days.

US-119-HR9681.title: Fair Seeds for Farmers Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9681.description: To amend the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act to limit intellectual property protection for plants, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9681.aiSummary: The bill would limit federal intellectual property protection for plants, plant varieties, and plant material that can be used to grow more plants, except under two existing plant law systems. It would also make contracts that block research, breeding, experimentation, seed saving, or propagation of that material unenforceable. The change would apply to patent applications already pending or filed after the bill becomes law, and to new agreements made after that date.

US-119-HR9043.title: Sex Trafficking Demand Reduction Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9043.description: To amend the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 relating to determinations with respect to efforts of foreign countries to reduce demand for commercial sex acts under the minimum standards for the elimination of trafficking.
US-119-HR9043.aiSummary: This bill would change how the U.S. judges foreign countries under the anti-trafficking law. It would add steps for countries to show serious efforts to stop buying commercial sex, teach buyers how traffickers exploit people in prostitution, and cut demand for sex tourism. The change would take effect on the date the bill becomes law and would apply to later country checks.
